{{nihongo|'''Oda Shrine (Ibaraki)'''|太田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Ōta Shrine''' (おおだじんじゃ / おおたじんじゃ<ref>“Ōda”: Osaka Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines and local place names in Osaka Prefecture; “Ōta”: Nihon no Kamigami.</ref>) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Ōta, {{ill|Ibaraki, Osaka|Q502403|qid=Q502403}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The current enshrined deities are the following three:
* {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Hayasusanō no Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami}}

As alternative theories regarding the enshrined deities, the *{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}* lists Sarutahiko Ōkami, while the *{{ill|Sesshū Gundan|Q11498591|qid=Q11498591}}* lists the three deities of Ise, Hachiman, and Sumiyoshi<ref name="神々"/>. In addition, because this area is thought to be the original homeland of the “Nakatomi Ōta no Muraji” recorded in the *{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}*<ref name="中臣大田連">*Shinsen Shōjiroku*, Settsu Province, Shinbetsu Tenshin, Nakatomi Ōta no Muraji entry.</ref>, there is also a theory that the original enshrined deity was {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane no Mikoto}}, the ancestral deity of the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|Q1198447|qid=Q1198447}}<ref name="神々"/>.

=== History ===
=== Founding ===
[[File:Oodakf13.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Ōta Chausuyama Kofun and shrine precincts<br />(the shrine grove is on the left side of the kofun)}}{{Small|{{National land aerial photography}}.}}]]
The date of founding is unknown. The shrine stands adjacent to the {{ill|Ōta Chausuyama Kofun|Q11444409|qid=Q11444409}} (the Misima Aino Mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|Q349277|qid=Q349277}}), and it is believed that the kofun existed before the founding of Ōta Shrine<ref name="神々">*Nihon no Kamigami*, Ōta Shrine entry.</ref>. Current archaeology holds that the true tomb of Emperor Keitai is the {{ill|Imashirozuka Kofun|Q11376795|qid=Q11376795}} to the northeast, and the relationship between Ōta Shrine and the Ōta Chausuyama Kofun—including the question of who is actually buried there—has been noted<ref name="神々"/>.

It is also thought to be the original homeland of the “Nakatomi Ōta no Muraji” recorded in the *{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}*<ref name="中臣大田連"/>, and there is a theory that rituals were conducted here by the Nakatomi Ōta clan<ref name="地名">*Osaka-fu no Chimei*, Ōta Village entry.</ref>. The *Shinsen Shōjiroku* states that the Nakatomi Ōta no Muraji were descendants of Mimashuku Sukune, a thirteenth-generation descendant of Ame-no-Koyane no Mikoto; this figure is sometimes identified with “Mimashi no Sukune no Mikoto” in the *Matsuo Shrine Genealogy* (there listed as a fourteenth-generation descendant), whose child “Ōta-hiko no Mikoto” is said to have led to the Nakatomi Ōta no Muraji<ref name="神々"/>.

Additionally, the *{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|Q11498726|qid=Q11498726}}*, Ibo District, Ōta Village entry, records that “Kure no Suguri moved from the Korean Peninsula to Ōta Village in {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}{{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}}, then split off and moved to Ōta Village in Mishima Kamigun, Settsu Province.” Although this area is generally considered to belong to {{ill|Shimashimo district|Q10976940|qid=Q10976940}}, which contradicts the mention of Mishima Kamigun ({{ill|Shimakami district|Q10965808|qid=Q10965808}}), the possession of the kabane title “Suguri” suggests immigration from Baekje<ref name="神々"/>. From this, a theory has been proposed that as the Nakatomi clan advanced into Mishima, they merged with descendants of these “Kure no Suguri,” forming the Nakatomi Ōta no Muraji, and that Ōta Shrine was founded as their clan shrine<ref name="神々"/>.

=== Overview ===
In the *{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed under {{ill|Shimashimo district|Q10976940|qid=Q10976940}}, Settsu Province, as “Ōta Shrine, Kuwabutsu”<ref>The Kujō family manuscript and Kongō-ji manuscript of the *Engishiki* record the name as “Ōda Shrine” (*Osaka-fu no Chimei*, Ōta Village entry).</ref>. This places it among the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and indicates that during the Kinensai festival the court presented hoes and quivers.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.
